claims.text: The initial alloy is equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance.
3D ink extrusion printing followed by hydrogen de-binding and titanium-sponge-gettered vacuum sintering will significantly reduce oxygen contamination during synthesis.
Hydrogen de-binding removes polymeric binders from the printed material.
Titanium-sponge gettering captures residual oxygen during vacuum sintering.
The proposed processing route will reduce the formation of deleterious oxide phases.
The proposed processing route will produce cleaner grain boundaries and a stabilized microstructure.
Reduced synthesis-stage oxygen contamination will decrease the formation of brittle oxides.
Cleaner processing will maintain microstructural features responsible for ductility and high-temperature strength.
The processed alloy will exhibit lower oxidation rates than cast HfNbTaTiZr during exposure at 1000 °C in air for about 100 hours.
The processed alloy will preserve tensile ductility similar to that of untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The processed alloy will preserve yield strength similar to that of untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed benefits are expected at 1000 °C in an oxidizing atmosphere for approximately 100 hours and under tensile strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1.
